help.help_panel.07: How everything works — and why — all in one place
help.help_panel.10: **Block start reminder**: speaks up when a block starts; can fire up to {join} minutes early (set in Settings; default is “on time”).
help.help_panel.12: **Block end reminder**: asks “done or not done?” when the block ends — Required blocks get a notification with buttons, so you can answer right there.
help.help_panel.14: **Review**: currently {reviewAt} {reviewActionLabel} (the default is to do nothing); you can also pick “Open Review” (only when you return to the app — it won't steal focus while you're working). (Change this in Settings.)
help.help_panel.16: **Pause reminders**: {QUIET_PRESET_MINUTES} minutes / {QUIET_PRESET_MINUTES2} hours / until “tomorrow morning” (the time is adjustable). While paused, reminders are **not shown, only logged silently**; resuming does not replay a backlog.
help.help_panel.20: **Wake the app on time after closing**: off by default — only when you explicitly turn it on does it register a task in Windows Task Scheduler (nothing runs in the background behind your back).
help.help_panel.23: What's measured is **time**: the time each block occupies in a day is added up; **overlapping / side-by-side blocks count only once**.
help.help_panel.28: against the adjustable **daily budget** (currently {budgetHours} hours; change it above): if a day goes over, its bar turns red + the top bar says a word + the tray gets a thin red ring.
help.help_panel.31: Tasks marked **⊘ (not counted)** don't count — the toggle lives on the Backlog row (or on the block itself for temp blocks).
help.help_panel.34: The numbers are just the time those timeline blocks take up — check them against your own count if you like.
help.help_panel.36: **Export a backup**: saves the whole database as one consistent copy (tasks / blocks / sequences / settings all included); put it on an external or cloud drive, your call.
help.help_panel.38: **Restore from a backup**: replaces the current data with the backup and **restarts automatically**; a “pre-restore copy” is kept first, so you can switch back if it wasn't right.
help.help_panel.42: **Export calendar (.ics)**: exports the whole schedule as a calendar file (finished and unfinished included); times are UTC — once imported into your phone / system calendar they show the **same moment in time**; importing the same file twice won't duplicate events.
help.help_panel.46: **Portable mode (off by default)**: when on, data (database / pre-restore copy / pending restore file) is written to the `data\` folder inside the app folder; copy the whole folder to a USB stick and take it with you (Export backup / .ics use the system “Save as”, so you choose where they go). When switching, the two data sets are **shown side by side** (location / last modified / size / tasks·blocks), and you pick which one to use; **the side that would be overwritten** gets a copy first (`before-switch`), while the other side is left untouched and never deleted. In portable mode “Reminder schedule” is unavailable.
help.help_panel.55: **A template is a week's skeleton**: layer / time slot / duration + **task name and category**; when applied, tasks with the same name are reused (new ones are only created if none exist), and only rows without a name become temporary blocks.
help.help_panel.59: The entry point is **Templates** at the top of the timeline: the top part applies one (lays it over the week you're viewing), the bottom part saves the current week as a template (you can delete rows first).
help.help_panel.62: **Suggestions**: once you've used it for {days} days, completed {done} times, and last week had at least 3 blocks, it asks at the top “Save last week as a template?” — **it asks once and never creates one behind your back**.
help.help_panel.66: **Weekly repeat**: add a rule (weekday + time) in a Backlog task's ⚙ — it's placed automatically when you open a week (the block shows a a **repeat mark**); the duration follows the task's **estimate** (30 minutes if empty); deleting a generated block means it won't be generated again this week, and the rule stays.
help.help_panel.71: You can change the thresholds under Settings → More → Features → Template suggestions; “don’t ask again” simply turns it off.
help.help_panel.73: **The first time you open an empty library**, a card appears in the lower left (three steps): ① write down one or two things to do today ② drag them into today's slots ③ click ✓ when done (a reminder fires when the time comes).
help.help_panel.75: Now and then a one-off hint appears at the top: **shown once, the first time you use a feature**, one at a time, and it never gets in the way.
help.help_panel.78: “Turn all off” switches off progressive hints; to bring them back: Settings → Guide & tutorials → “Reopen progressive hints”.
help.help_panel.79: **You can always get back to the tutorials from Settings → Guide & tutorials**: the guide, the first-run card, and the progressive-hints switch.
help.help_panel.81: **The key table lives in the “Keys” panel opened with `?`** (Settings → Alerts & controls → “Keys…” also opens it) — it is not duplicated here.
help.help_panel.83: To add a task fast: press **C** in the timeline — Backlog expands and the cursor lands in “Add a task…” (pressing c inside an input isn't hijacked).
help.help_panel.86: Every feature added in v2 can be tucked away in Settings; **turning one off only hides the UI and behavior — it never deletes data** (merged blocks, linked sequences and saved templates all stay as they are), and turning it back on restores everything.

help.help_panel.97: **Window state** (size, position, maximized) lives in the system app-config folder (`%APPDATA%`) and does **not** follow `data\` in portable mode — copying the folder to another machine will not carry the window position with it.
help.help_panel.98: **Time & date**: change them under Settings → Timeline. “Follow system” uses the language default; custom short date/time patterns set in Windows can’t be read by WebView (platform limitation) — pick a fixed style (dashes / slashes / long) if you want one. The UI language’s “Follow system” picks Chinese / English from the system language; **changing the system language while the app is running takes effect after a restart**. The UI ships with Chinese / English only: any other system language falls back to English (you can pin Chinese in Settings).
help.help_panel.100: **Night hours and dimming**: in Settings → Appearance you can set a pair of night hours (default 22:00 → 06:00). “By time” uses dark during them; with “Dim non-working hours” on, the timeline dims them too (looks only — no data is touched). For hours past midnight, just write 22:00 → 06:00.

ui.sanity_settings.124: Light / dark follows the Windows setting. Changes apply right away.
ui.sanity_settings.129: Each thumbnail is a mini interface in that scheme (following your current light/dark mode): accent, block fill and background at a glance. Changes apply right away and stick after a restart.
ui.sanity_settings.131: When off, that left bar is invisible (the colour blends into the block) — clicking the left edge still switches layers, and reminders and bulk layer changes are unaffected.
ui.sanity_settings.133: Draws a 2-pixel category stripe along the bottom of blocks (off by default). Colors only — no behavior changes.

help.help_panel.101: **Key bindings are customizable**: in Settings → “Keys…”, click a keycap and press the new key. Esc / Enter / Tab / arrow keys / Space / X / Ctrl+Z manage operations (pick up / drop / undo) and **cannot be changed**; one action, one key; letters are case-sensitive (Shift+T and T are different combos).
help.help_panel.102: **UI font**: under Settings → “Text & density” there are five options — Default (YaHei UI), Song (SimSun), Kai (KaiTi), DengXian and Monospace. It only changes interface type: Latin letters and digits still use the system UI font, and only Chinese characters use the chosen family. All five come with the system and nothing extra ships with the app.
